name: Bain de Soleil

card.summary: Discontinued 1925-born French-American tanning gel brand known for low SPF and nostalgia; no clinical evidence behind it.
card.note: Low-SPF tanning products offer limited sunburn protection by design.

lead: Bain de Soleil (French for "sun bath") was a tanning and sun care brand best known for Orange Gelee, a tinted gel, and for low-SPF products. People used it to deepen and speed up a sun tan and to get a bronzed, glowing look on the skin; its advertising sold the "St. Tropez tan." [1][2]

Wikipedia dates the brand to 1925, when a Paris perfumer developed an orange-gel tanning formula, and says it reached the US in the 1940s through Lanvin. [1] Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, names the creator as the hairdresser Antoine Cierplikowski, known as Monsieur Antoine, whose clients included Coco Chanel. [2] Bayer discontinued the brand in December 2019. [1]
No clinical studies of the brand are known. A 1981 hairless-mouse study compared seven sunscreens' protective effects on skin, and whether this brand was among them is not stated. [3]

chain: Tinted gel gives instant bronze color
Low SPF allows tanning while giving some protection
angle.text: The gel's tint colors the skin at once while the low SPF lets the sun darken it over time, which is how fans of the brand achieved a bronzed look. Low-SPF tanning products give limited protection by design.

infobox: Orange Gelee, SPF 4 in later years [1]

paras: Per Wikipedia, the product originated as an orange gel in Paris in 1925 and reached the US through Lanvin. Procter and Gamble owned it until Pfizer bought it in August 1995, and Pfizer sold it to Schering-Plough in October 1999. Bayer is listed as owner at discontinuation in December 2019. [1]

Grokipedia reports that the brand rose to prominence in the US in the 1970s and 1980s with a memorable jingle and Orange Gelee SPF 4, that Charles of the Ritz acquired US rights in 1963, that Procter and Gamble acquired it in 1988, and that Merck sold its consumer care unit including Coppertone and Bain de Soleil to Bayer in 2014. It also mentions fans petitioning for its return and a company announcing plans in November 2024 to relaunch it. These details come from an AI-generated source and are unconfirmed. [2]

sections.h: Products and use in tanning culture
paras: Wikipedia's account says the brand focused on low-SPF products for people who wanted to tan and was affiliated with Coppertone, with a final lineup including Orange Gelee SPF 4, Spray Transpare SPF 10 and Mega Tan SPF 4. Its 1970s and 1980s TV ads used the slogan "Bain de Soleil, for the St. Tropez tan." [1] Versions from SPF 4 to SPF 30 were sold in the late 1990s. [1]

No studies found. Related laboratory work includes a 1981 hairless-mouse study comparing seven sunscreens' protective factors against UVB effects on epidermal DNA synthesis; the brand is not identified among them. [3]

timeline.event: Orange-gel tanning formula developed in Paris. [1]
Brand introduced in the US through Lanvin. [1]
Pfizer acquires the brand from Procter and Gamble. [1]

quick.overview:
Bain de Soleil was a tanning-oriented sun care brand, famous for an orange gel launched in Paris in 1925.

Bayer discontinued it in December 2019.
quick.mechanism: It was positioned as a tanning aid with low SPF rather than a high-protection sunscreen.
quick.risks: No brand-specific studies were found. Low-SPF products give correspondingly lower sunburn protection.
